messages:
maria (Finance): FYI we just got the new cloud invoice. GPU unit costs in us-west spiked ~33% this billing cycle. I ran a quick pass on unit economics and margin impact — we need to discuss reserved commitments vs packaging changes this week. @dan can infra do any quick mitigations?

dan (Eng-Infra): seeing it too. A handful of preemptible pools drained overnight in us-west. We can shift some jobs to us-east or asia for cheaper capacity but latency-sensitive routes are pinned. Also possible to push more to dedicated reserved instances if we commit.

maria (Finance): rough numbers from my sheet: ```prev_gpu_hour = $0.18
new_gpu_hour = $0.24
throughput = 1.2M tokens/hr/GPU
cost_per_token_prev = prev_gpu_hour / throughput = $0.00000015
cost_per_token_new = new_gpu_hour / throughput = $0.00000020
delta ≈ +33% -> hosted gross margin hit ≈ 4.5% absolute``` These are high-level — need better model but gives direction.

kevin (Finance): if those deltas hold, absorbing it lowers gross margin ~4-6% depending on mix. Passing 10% price to customers recovers >100% of the hit for hosted but will increase churn risk. Also reserved 1yr commit with volume could reduce unit cost by ~18-22% (cloud quote).

sanjay (Product): two knobs: 1) packaging/pricing change (raise hosted price or add a small surcharge) 2) new commitment product ('Committed Saver' or similar) to incentivize longer-term contracts and stabilize unit economics. Which is lower friction?

elaine (Eng-SRE): operationally we can: add region fallback routing to send non-pinned traffic to cheaper regions, enable aggressive batching for background workloads, and tighten cache TTLs. All doable but we must flag customers with region pinning and latency SLOs.

dan (Eng-Infra): technical caveat: shifting to other regions will increase inter-region egress for some customers and complicate data residency. Also need to ensure we have enough reserved quota in target regions before moving.

maria (Finance): action items proposal: 1) kevin run margin sims for three scenarios (absorb / pass 5% / pass 10% + reserved commit options) 2) dan/elaine produce a list of traffic that can be region-shifted and estimate delta latency & egress cost 3) product (sanjay) draft 2 packaging options: small price bump vs committed discount product 4) sales to flag top-50 pinned customers and communication plan.

kevin (Finance): on it — I'll put a model up by EOD and share a short spreadsheet: https://tiny.example.com/rrc-gpu-model (working link, will lock later). I'll include sensitivity to throughput changes and quantization adoption.

cap-bot: Capacity Planner updated: Reserved slot request queued for us-east (100 GPUs) — expected procurement ETA 7 days.

sanjay (Product): quick thought: offer a limited-time 15% committed discount for 6 months (auto-renew opt-in) to move customers off spot/hosted burst into predictable capacity. Could be marketed as 'cost-stability' add-on.

maria (Finance): good. Also please model worst-case where spot prices stay +30% for 3 months. We should prepare an internal comms doc for execs with recommended path and customer impact numbers.

elaine (Eng-SRE): I'll start a map of customers with region pins and latency SLOs and post in #eng-sre. We should coordinate on any automated region shift experiments behind feature flags.

kevin (Finance): will share sims by EOD. After that, propose a decision meeting tomorrow 10:30am to pick between temporary surcharge vs push-to-commit strategy.

maria (Finance): thanks all — priority is margin protection without breaking core SLAs. :eyes: We'll keep options open but need a recommendation for execs tomorrow.

dan (Eng-Infra): one last note — if we do a 1yr commit, negotiate convertible options (start small, scale up) so we don't overcommit if demand shifts.

kevin (Finance): noted. I'll add commit size sensitivity to the model.

maria (Finance): closing thread for now — followups in the decision meeting.
